the rate of glutathione conjugating activity in the liver is dependent on the glutathione concentration and is only decreased at severe depletion of hepatic glutathoine.
glutathione conjugating capacity is not a limiting factor for the biliary excretory rate of the glutthione conjugate of BIU in the rat in the physiological situation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the rate of glutathione conjugating enzymes in the liver of rats is not affected by a decrease in the liver glutathione concentration, as long as the liver glutathoine concentration is not below 0.5-0.7 mumol/g of wet liver.
the hepatic conjugation rate of BIU in rats is dependent on glutathione content only when this is very low, i.e. at a glutathione content below 0.5-1 mmol/g of liver.
the hepatic conjugation of BIU is not a limiting step in the biotransformation and elimination of the substrate in the rat in the conditions of our experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the glutathione depletion in the rat liver is not a major factor in determining the rate of hepatic glutathionylation of BIU.
